trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any concrete OpenAI IPO/S-1 headline accompanies the probability move or whether it is pure market noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT intraday move vs. Nasdaq to see if any idiosyncratic reaction is visible above beta.
time_plan.2h: Scan newswires (Bloomberg/Reuters) for OpenAI corporate-structure or fundraising news confirming a real information event.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the prediction-market move persisted or reverted; if reverted, treat as noise.
time_plan.12h: Log realized MSFT return vs. prediction; note whether any public IPO confirmation emerged.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large economic stake in OpenAI, so a shift in the market-implied probability of an OpenAI IPO is the closest listed proxy. However, the sign is ambiguous: a rising IPO probability could unlock value/mark-to-market gains for MSFT's stake, but it could also complicate the commercial relationship or dilute MSFT's preferential access. An IPO is a slow structural corporate event, not a catalyst that moves a mega-cap's price sharply within 12h. Expected move is well below the 700bps tradable threshold.

predictions.reasoning: A rising probability of an OpenAI public listing could be read as bullish sentiment for the AI investment cycle broadly, lifting AI-thematic baskets. But the linkage is diffuse and second-order: OpenAI is private, the ETF holds hardware/semis/software names with only indirect exposure, and IPO timing news rarely produces a same-day thematic repricing of 700bps. Direction and magnitude are both uncertain, so this is a non-tradable, low-conviction mapping.

uncertainty_notes: The sign of the effect on MSFT is genuinely ambiguous (value unlock vs. relationship/dilution risk).
Prediction-market probability moves on a 2026 event have little reason to translate into sharp 12h moves in liquid assets.

The market is mislabeled 'elections' which suggests low data quality.

llm_justification.summary: This market prices the probability OpenAI does NOT go public by end-2026. There is no direct liquid proxy for OpenAI; the closest listed exposures are Microsoft (large stakeholder) and broad AI-thematic ETFs. Both mappings are weak: the directional sign is ambiguous, IPO timing is a slow structural event unlikely to move mega-caps or thematic baskets by the 700bps tradable threshold within 12 hours, and prediction-market noise on a 2026 resolution rarely reflects imminent public information. We therefore assign 'unclear' direction and low confidence, with sub-threshold expected magnitudes — this is not a tradable signal.
key_assumptions: Microsoft retains a material economic interest in OpenAI.
No public S-1 filing or concrete IPO announcement has occurred at the time of the signal.
Prediction-market probability moves here are largely noise absent a corroborating headline.
failure_modes: The probability move simply reflects public speculation already priced into equities (no leak).
MSFT's reaction, if any, could be the opposite sign to what an 'IPO more likely' read implies.
Proxies (MSFT, BOTZ) are so diversified that OpenAI-specific news is drowned out by macro/beta.
An IPO event, even if signaled, is months/years away and creates no 12h catalyst.
Market is potentially miscategorized/low-liquidity, making the implied probability unreliable.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
